title: Aftershift Flux Notes
content:
Shift window: 2025-11-03 22:00 PST -> 2025-11-04 06:00 PST
Owner: Jordan Reyes (night) — handoff to Maya Patel at 06:00
Context: Evening traffic surge from APAC region. Two transient incidents (latency + degraded-quality rollouts) observed; mostly mitigated but left some temporary workarounds that need follow-up.

Quick summary:
- 22:45 — Alert: p50 generation latency crossing 550ms on hosted-api-prod (route: /v1/generate). Pager triggered.
- 23:03 — Autoscale responded, but tail latencies persisted for >12m. KV cache hit rates dropped on model-quantx-3 (suspected cache invalidation).
- 00:15 — Degraded quality reports (few customer complaints) correlated to a canary rollout of model-qa-1.2 in region-eu. Canary stopped and rolled back at 00:25.
- 01:10 — Sched: temporary traffic re-route applied for heavy customers to dedicated pool; mitigated latency.

What I did (actions & commands):
- Checked Prometheus dashboards: redwood/api/generation_latency_p50, p95. Confirmed spike.
- Confirmed increased queue length on worker nodes: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep quantx
- Forced a cache warm (TTL reset) for quantx shard 7: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/cache/flush?shard=7 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Temporarily reverted the canary rollout: POST to console rollouts API to rollback model-qa-1.2 -> model-qa-1.1 (request id: rlt-20251103-0040).
- Rerouted two high-QPS customers: PATCH routing-policy id=rt-89 set target=dedicated-pool-east-2 (see JIRA-MLINF-237 for change request).
- Notified customers in #cust-notify channel with brief apology and link to status page.

Temporary workarounds left in place (must be validated / removed during daytime):
1) Routing override for customers: rt-89 and rt-94 -> dedicated-pool-east-2 (manual override).
   - Reason: reduce p95 for hosted pool while we investigate cache invalidation pattern.
   - Action for next shift: verify dedicated pool load (expected ~30% extra). If steady for >12h, file capacity request.
2) Cache flush for quantx shard 7 performed; monitor hit-rate for 6h.
   - Metric to watch: redwood/cache/hit_rate{shard="7"} (alert if < 0.75 for more than 15m).
3) Canary rollback completed for model-qa-1.2. Canary artifacts left in s3://canaries/model-qa-1.2/ (don't re-promote until postmortem).

Open items / follow-up (priority ordered):
- P1: Root cause of cache invalidations: hypothesis that scheduled background job (metadata-reindexer) was iterating over shards and triggered cascade TTL resets. Ticket assigned: CONFS-8421 — need logs for reindexer runs between 22:00–23:30 and correlation with cache TTL events.
- P2: Investigate autoscaler configuration: p95 target seems too permissive for bursty APAC traffic. Suggested change: add short-term burst capacity policy (scale cooldown 30s -> 10s). Create RFC.
- P3: Improve canary observations: add quality-check harness to automated canary job; sourcetest failing to catch latent regressions in model-qa-1.2.
- P4: Customer follow-ups: Ops to send a short incident note to affected customers; CS already drafted message (#cust-notify). Confirm final wording with legal if quoting SLA credits.

Diagnostic checklist (what to run if it recurs):
- Prometheus quick queries:
  - generation latency: sum(rate(redwood_api_generation_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route)
  - queue length: redwood_worker_queue_length{instance=~".*quantx.*"}
- Check worker health: kubectl -n inference describe pod <pod> | grep -E "OOMKilled|RestartCount"
- Inspect cache metrics: redis-cli -h $CACHE_HOST INFO keyspace or use control-plane endpoint: GET /cache/metrics?shard=<n>
- Validate model routing: curl -s $CONTROL_PLANE/routes | jq '.routes[] | select(.id=="rt-89")'
- If dedicated pool under strain: scale up via infra CLI: infractl scale pool --name dedicated-pool-east-2 --delta 2gpus --reason "night surge"

Quick recovery knobs (use with caution):
- Rollback canary (console rollouts API) — we already did this; use idempotently.
- Apply routing override to move heavy customers to dedicated pools.
- Temporarily reduce max_seq_length for model-quantx-3 for non-critical customers to cut per-token latency: update model config (careful: affects output).
- Enable cheaper model fallback: route to quantized variant quantx-3-q4 in low-latency policy.

Notes to next shift (Maya):
- Verify routing overrides (rt-89/rt-94) removed only after dedicated pool CPU/GPU < 75% for a sustained 1h.
- Check shard 7 cache hit-rate at 06:30 and 09:00; if <0.75 after the 6h window, escalate to Applied ML (Evan).
- Pull logs for reindexer runs CONFS-8421 and attach to ticket. I left a grep filter saved as /home/jordan/bin/reindexer-log-extract.sh (copy to your account if needed).
- Draft a short blameless postmortem skeleton: start with timeline (22:40–00:30) and three action items (cache hardening, autoscale tuning, canary checks).

Parking lot / ideas (non-urgent):
- Consider per-shard rolling TTLs so a single reindex iterate doesn't nuke whole cache.
- Blue/green canary with synthetic eval harness that measures quality delta before traffic ramp.
- Add an SLO-derived alarm that couples quality regressions with user-visible errors (not just model-internal metrics).

Things I scribbled to self (notes-to-self):
- "If see p95 >1.2s, first check routing overrides — they mask root cause."
- "Cache flush helped but might reoccur when reindexer runs — coordinate with infra team next week."
- "Remember to zip logs for CONFS-8421, limit size to 50MB."

Files / locations pulled during triage:
- Logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/2025-11-03/infra/*quantx*.log
- Canaries: s3://canaries/model-qa-1.2/
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/production-gen?orgId=1&from=now-6h

If you need me: ping @jordan.reyes (Slack) or call cell: +1-415-555-0198 — but prefer Slack unless critical.

End of notes.

-- Jordan (night)
